title: Incremental output crediting and quota reconciliation for resumed/partial streams
creator: Anika Sharma
description: Investigate and implement a deterministic, audit-friendly approach to crediting output tokens and enforcing quotas when streaming responses are resumed, partially replayed, or split across segments. Current gaps: double-counting on reconnects, undercounting when clients request suffix-only data, and inconsistent attribution between ingress (input tokens) and egress (generated tokens) for multi-part responses. Goal is to produce a single reconciliation algorithm, tests, and monitoring to ensure billing correctness across all streaming edge cases.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Triage: Ticket created after customer incident where resumed stream incurred duplicated billing. Attached initial reproducer and sample trace from prod-logs-2025-02-10.

2025-02-17 - Engineering sync: Agreed to prototype a 'stream-consensus' proof-of-concept in a sandbox runtime. Trade-off: do we encode chunk provenance in chunk IDs (adds header bytes) vs rely on server-side idempotency windows (more stateful). Decided to prototype both approaches.

2025-02-24 - Design review: PM and Billing team prefer server-side canonical attribution that does not require client upgrades. Scoped prototype to: (1) deterministic chunk hashing + sequence GUID, (2) server-side resume detection using session nonce + last-acked offset.

2025-03-01 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5423 implements chunk GUID and proof-of-dup detection. Needs integration tests and a reconciliation job to correct historical mismatches.

2025-03-04 - Observability: Added temporary dashboard tile (dash: Billing -> Stream-Reconnect-Anomalies) to track events where resume_request != last_acked_offset. Initial run shows ~0.03% of streaming sessions affected.

2025-03-05 - Blocker found: partial suffix requests from some SDKs intentionally ask for 'tail only' and expect resumed generation; chunk-GUID approach would change wire format. Decision: default to server-side detection + opt-in explicit chunk GUID header for a future protocol version.
Follow-ups: schedule migration plan with SDK teams, add nightly reconciliation job to find and correct 1-hour windows of duplicate credits, update billing docs and support playbook.
acceptance_criteria: Server detects resumed/overlapping stream segments without relying on a new client wire format for >=99.99% of cases in our current traffic patterns.
No duplicate egress token credits for resumed sessions in the compensated test harness (repro stack) across 10k synthetic sessions.
Reconciliation job can identify and correct historical duplicate credits for a specified time window and emit an audit report suitable for finance and customer support.
New monitoring dashboard surfaces resume-related anomalies and a PagerDuty alert when duplicate-credit rate > 0.1% for 5 minutes.
Design and rollout notes published to confluence at https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/METER/stream-resume-metering
test_plan: Unit tests for chunk-dedup and resume-detection logic (edge offsets, partial suffix, client-initiated rewind).
End-to-end integration test in staging using repro harness: simulate 50k streaming sessions with randomized disconnect/hang/reconnect patterns and assert token accounting invariants.
Reconciliation job dry-run against a 7-day historical sample to measure fix rates and false positives before enabling auto-correction.
Performance test: confirm CPU/memory overhead of resume-detection < 1% at p50 and p95 for typical request loads.
SDK compatibility smoke tests: ensure no existing SDKs break when server emits resume-metadata in streaming frames.
Billing QA: cross-check reconciled records with existing token-usage exports and internal billing ledger for 100 sample sessions.
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (non-invasive): implement server-side resume detection using session nonce + last-acked offset stored in short-lived state (TTL 2 hours). Emit 'resume_detected' event to metering pipeline and suppress duplicate egress credits when overlap > threshold.
Phase 2 (opt-in protocol): define 'chunk-guid' header to be emitted by SDKs to achieve deterministic attribution; keep backwards compatibility by ignoring header if absent.

Reconciliation job: map stream event fingerprints (session, client_ip_hash, model_id, timestamps) to token credits and find clusters likely to be duplicates. Provide an override list for finance team to accept/reject batch corrections.
Store a immutability-hash for each final billed record to aid audits. Use the existing metering-store S3 bucket path 'metering/reconciliations/YYYY-MM-DD'.

Data retention: keep raw stream events for 90 days for reconciliation; derived billing records retained per finance policy. Add a note to Privacy/Compliance about the extended retention for debugging.
Risk: server-side state increases memory pressure on frontends. Mitigation: keep only metadata (8 bytes session pointer + 32 bit offset) and use LRU eviction + soft TTL.
PRs: runtime#5423 (chunk GUID PoC), metering#298 (resume event schema), reconciliation#12 (job scaffolding).
rollout_plan: Canary: enable resume-detection in a small fleet (region us-east-1, 1% traffic) for 48 hours. Monitor the duplicate-credit rate and error logs.
Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 7 days if no regressions. Each step gated by automated checks in the deploy pipeline.
Reconciliation: run dry-run mode for 72 hours post-100% rollout to surface historical anomalies before applying auto-corrections.
Customer comms: prepare support template and opt-in reimbursement pathway for any customers impacted by prior overbilling discovered by the reconciliation job.
SDK migration: publish guidelines and timeline for chunk-guid adoption; default behavior remains compatible for 6 months.
monitoring: Dashboards: Billing -> Stream Reconciler Overview, showing duplicate-credit rate, resume-detection rate, reconciliation fix count.
SLOs: target duplicate-credit contribution to billed tokens < 0.01% daily.
Alerts: P1 Pager when duplicate-credit rate > 0.1% for 5 minutes or reconciliation job failure.
Audit logs: store reconciliation job diffs to 'billing-audit' and link them to incident IDs for customer disputes.
